items.title: De Ouaga à Bittou, une nuit sur le front de la lutte contre la contrebande avec le DG des Douanes
items.description: Dimanche 30 août 2026. Il est 12 heures. Tandis que les Ouagalais partagent leurs derniers verres autour des poulets flambés avant la reprise, la cour de la Direction générale des Douanes, elle, est en mouvement. ​Des pick-up armés sont positionnés. Le visage masqué, le casque ajusté, des agents contrôlent une ultime fois leur matériel tactique. L'heure est au départ. Destination : Bittou. ​Dès les consignes de départ données, le cortège s'ébranle sous la conduite du Directeur de la Surveillance du territoire (DST). Avand de prendre la route, les dernières consignes sont données -©Faso7 Quelques heures plus tard, le Directeur général des Douanes en personne, le Dr Yves Kafando, prend à son tour la route en direction de cette commune frontalière. ​Il est 22h10 lorsque le patron de la douane arrive sur les lieux. Quelle urgence justifie une telle descente nocturne ? ​Deux mois auparavant, le Dr Yves Kafando s'était déjà rendu à Bittou pour échanger avec les exportateurs et martelé la nécessité de mettre fin à la fraude. Message pas entendu Venu mesurer l'impact de sa sensibilisation, le constat qu'il dresse sur place est sans appel : le message n'a pas été entendu. ​Sur le terrain, les douaniers mettent au jour plusieurs habitations transformées en entrepôts clandestins de marchandises de contrebande. Le DG Yves Kafando constate l'ampleur de la fraude -©Faso7 À mesure que les cadenas sautent sous les coups des agents, le DG constate l'ampleur des dégâts : des milliers de sacs d'engrais, des herbicides et pesticides non homologués, des stocks d'huile, de riz, mais aussi des cartons de comprimés, d'injectables et d'amphétamines. ​Toutes ces marchandises étaient dissimulées dans ces magasins d'infortune, prêtes à être injectées frauduleusement sur le marché national. « Que les fraudeurs le sachent… » Un fléau que l'administration douanière s'engage à éradiquer pour assainir la concurrence, préserver l'économie et protéger la santé des populations. « Que les fraudeurs le sachent : nous sommes en temps de révolution. Quel que soit le moment où ils commettent leurs forfaits, de jour comme de nuit, la douane burkinabè sera debout pour y mettre un terme. Aux agents des douanes, j'appelle à une vigilance renforcée, car c'est la condition indispensable pour éradiquer ces pratiques néfastes » a martelé le Directeur général. ​Le succès de ce coup de filet repose sur la précision du renseignement douanier, mais aussi sur une synergie d'action avec les forces armées. Une collaboration que le DG a tenu à saluer vivement. ​« C'est l'occasion pour moi de remercier le Régiment militaire de Tenkodogo, qui nous a accompagnés pour que cette mission se déroule dans les meilleures conditions », a-t-il soutenu. ​L'offensive ne s'arrête pas là. Alors qu'une dizaine d'entrepôts ont déjà été ciblés, le DG a ordonné la poursuite des fouilles. L'ensemble des produits saisis sera convoyé vers Ouagadougou dans les prochains jours. ​Ses consignes transmises aux troupes déployées, le patron des douanes reprend immédiatement la route. 240 kilomètres à parcourir en pleine nuit pour regagner la capitale. Dès lundi matin, d'autres dossiers l'attendent car « tout est urgent » dans un Burkina Faso en pleine Révolution Progressiste Populaire. items.title: Koosin : VDP et populations mobilisés pour désherber les champs des VDP et de l’école de Zékuy
items.description: BURKINA-KOOSIN-AGRICULTURE Koosin : VDP et populations mobilisés pour désherber les champs des VDP et de l’école de Zékuy Doumbala, 29 août 2026 (AIB)-Plus de 130 personnes, composées de Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP) et de parents d’élèves, se sont mobilisées ce samedi 29 août 2026 pour désherber les champs des VDP et de l’école de Zékuy, dans la commune de Doumbala. Dans la matinée, une forte mobilisation s’est déployée dans les deux champs afin de les débarrasser des mauvaises herbes. Munis de dabas, les participants ont commencé les travaux par le champ des Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP). Après cette première étape, les volontaires se sont dirigés vers le champ scolaire de Zékuy dans une ambiance de solidarité et de motivation, pour le désherbage des plants de maïs. Le président du conseil, Timothée Diarra, s’est réjoui de la forte mobilisation et selon lui, cette participation massive témoigne de l’entente et de la franche collaboration entre les populations. « Si les gens sont sortis si nombreux, c’est une preuve d’entente et de franche collaboration. Cela prouve que les populations ont compris et adhèrent à la vision de la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP) », a-t-il déclaré. Au terme des travaux, le directeur de l’école de Zékuy, Jean-Bosco Traoré, a exprimé sa reconnaissance aux participants pour leur mobilisation en faveur de l’établissement. « Je vous suis reconnaissant pour votre adhésion massive à la cause de l’école. La production de ce champ sera d’un grand soutien aux besoins de l’école », a-t-il indiqué. Agence d’information du Burkina LD/AC/HB/OO

items.title: IHC dismisses 3 petitions from Adiala prisoners seeking private hospital treatment, communication with relatives abroad
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Monday dismissed petitions filed by three Adiala Jail prisoners seeking treatment at private hospitals and permission to communicate with relatives abroad, similar to the relief granted to PTI founder Imran Khan. Justice Muhammad Asif issued separate written judgments after reserving the verdict on August 27 on petitions filed by prisoners Owais Altaf, Muhammad Ilyas Khan and Muhammad Ismail Hussain, holding that imprisonment restricted a person’s liberty in accordance with the law but did not create a right to every facility of choice. The petitions assumed significance after the Supreme Court (SC) on Aug 18 directed the authorities to transfer PTI founder Imran Khan to Shifa International Hospital for medical examination and treatment. The three prisoners subsequently approached the IHC seeking similar relief. Altaf and Ilyas had sought permission to obtain treatment at private hospitals, claiming that the required medical facilities were not available within the government hospital system. Meanwhile, Hussain sought permission to communicate with his brother living abroad through WhatsApp. During the hearing, the petitioners’ counsel argued that one of the prisoners was suffering from a serious bleeding disorder and had developed internal bleeding in the large intestine, which could become life-threatening. He said that the prisoner had remained incarcerated for around six months and had repeatedly been taken to the hospital. In its written order, the IHC held that imprisonment meant restrictions on freedom according to law, and that “every technical facility cannot be declared a fundamental right”. A prisoner, it said, has no legal right to be transferred to a private hospital of his choice. The court observed that the primary responsibility for prisoners’ treatment rested with the state’s administrative structure and government hospitals. It said that Rule 197 of the Pakistan Prison Rules provides a mechanism for moving a prisoner to a hospital outside the facility where necessary. “However, where treatment is not possible at a government hospital, the authorities can consider transferring a prisoner to a private medical facility on the recommendation of a medical board,” the court ruled. The IHC also considered the petitioners’ reliance on the SC’s order concerning Imran. It observed that there was no doubt that SC decisions were binding on the High Courts, but noted that the Aug 18 directions were interim in nature and the matter referred to by the petitioners was still pending before the SC. The interim order, therefore, could not be treated as a final decision creating a general legal right for every prisoner to seek treatment at a private hospital of their own choice, the IHC held. The court directed the jail administration to continue providing all necessary medical facilities to the prisoners in accordance with law. The court also dismissed the petition regarding Hussain’s request to communicate with his brother abroad through WhatsApp. It noted that the petitioner had failed to establish that the jail administration’s Aug 2 order was illegal or that his fundamental rights had been violated. The court, however, observed that if WhatsApp, video calls or any other lawful means of communication were available to prisoners, the competent authorities could consider such requests in accordance with prison discipline, security requirements and the Pakistan Prison Rules 1978. During the hearing, the Punjab Advocate General Barrister Zafarullah had maintained that the authorities would act strictly in accordance with the law and prison rules. Islamabad’s Advocate General Naveed Hayat Malik and jail authorities also appeared before the court.

items.title: University of Memphis has not terminated scholarship deal with GSA – Director-General
items.description: The Ghana Scholarships Authority (GSA) has rejected a media report claiming that the University of Memphis has terminated its scholarship agreement with the Authority over an alleged $4 million debt. GSA Director-General Alex Kwaku Asafo-Agyei said the agreement, signed in April 2023, remains in force and provides for a five-year term ending in 2028, unless either party terminates it in accordance with the agreed terms. He explained that the agreement requires either party seeking to terminate the arrangement to give the other party 90 days’ prior written notice. According to him, no official or unofficial notice of termination has been served on the GSA, nor have there been discussions suggesting that the agreement has been terminated or is in the process of being terminated. Mr Asafo-Agyei further disclosed that the government, through the Ministry of Finance and following advice from the GSA, released $500,000 to the University of Memphis on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, as part-payment towards outstanding financial arrears. He said the GSA has also engaged the Ministry of Finance over the outstanding budgetary allocation needed to service the debt. The GSA Director-General, who is currently in the United States for a scheduled engagement with the University of Memphis, said discussions are underway to develop a roadmap for settling the outstanding financial obligations under what he described as a legacy debt partly inherited from his predecessor.

items.title: Police teargas pensioners protesting pension arrears at Lagos House
items.description: Police officers have reportedly fired teargas at pensioners protesting at the Lagos House in Ikeja over unpaid pension increases, wage awards and other outstanding benefits. The protesters, comprising members of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners (NUP) and retirees under the Contributory Pension Scheme, gathered at the government premises on Monday to demand action from the Lagos State Government. The pensioners called for the implementation of approved pension increases and wage awards, as well as the payment of outstanding pension arrears and other entitlements they said had remained unpaid. The demonstration was disrupted after police officers reportedly fired teargas at the retirees, forcing some of them to flee the premises. The action reportedly heightened tension at the scene, with the pensioners expressing dissatisfaction over the use of force against them while they were seeking payment of their entitlements. The retirees maintained that their protest was focused on the implementation of pension-related increases, payment of accumulated arrears and other benefits owed to them by the state government. The protest came after the pensioners had issued an August 31 deadline to the Lagos State Government to address their demands, particularly the outstanding pension enhancement and wage award. The retirees had warned that they would take further action if the government failed to meet the deadline. Their latest demonstration was aimed at drawing attention to what they described as prolonged delays in the payment of their entitlements and pressing the state government to resolve the issues affecting their welfare. The pensioners have repeatedly argued that delays in receiving their benefits have placed many retirees under financial pressure, particularly amid rising living costs. Monday’s protest at Lagos House, however, ended in disruption after the reported deployment of teargas by the police. items.title: Kloto : Mgr Amekuse Yawo Edmond prend possession du siège épiscopal de Kpalimé
items.description: Kpalimé, 31 août (ATOP) – Le nouvel évêque du diocèse de Kpalimé, Mgr Amékusé Yawo Edmond, ordonné le samedi 29 août, a officiellement pris possession de son siège épiscopal le dimanche 30 août à Kpalimé, au cours d’une messe pontificale à la cathédrale. Cette célébration marque le début officiel de son ministère pastoral à la tête du diocèse. Dans son homélie, Mgr Amékusé Yawo Edmond a insisté sur l’importance de l’obéissance envers Dieu qu’il a présentée comme un signe de communion et de disponibilité à cheminer ensemble. « L’obédience n’est pas seulement une simple formalité protocolaire, elle est un langage silencieux, une parole sans mot », a-t-il déclaré, estimant qu’elle traduit « la communion, la disponibilité à marcher ensemble » pour conduire l’Église-famille de Dieu à Kpalimé. Le nouvel évêque a invité les fidèles à préserver l’unité du diocèse malgré la diversité des convictions. « La richesse de notre diocèse, ce ne sont pas d’abord ses structures ou ses moyens, ce sont ses enfants. « C’est vous, c’est chacun de nous », a-t-il affirmé. S’appuyant sur l’Évangile selon saint Matthieu (Mt 16, 21-27), Mgr Amékusé Yawo Edmond a expliqué que la réaction de l’apôtre Pierre à l’annonce de la passion du Christ traduit la tendance humaine à vouloir éviter l’épreuve et l’échec. Selon lui, la souffrance peut cependant constituer un chemin de maturation et de croissance spirituelle. « La croix n’est pas une folie, elle est la sagesse de Dieu ; elle n’est pas une défaite, elle est une victoire de l’amour ; elle n’est pas une humiliation, elle est la porte de la gloire », a-t-il souligné. Auparavant, le nouvel évêque a pris place pour la première fois sur le siège épiscopal, symbole de son autorité pastorale et de sa mission. Les prêtres diocésains et religieux en service dans le diocèse, les religieux et religieuses ainsi que les fidèles laïcs présents lui ont tour à tour fait obédience. Plusieurs personnalités, telles que Prof. Dodzi Kokoroko, ministre en charge de l’Environnement, Général Dadja Maganawé, gouverneur de la région des Plateaux, des députés et sénateurs ont assisté à la messe. Y étaient également présents des chefs traditionnels et des membres de la commission d’organisation de la fête Dzawuza. ATOP/AYH/MD/BV

items.title: Journée internationale des personnes d'ascendance africaine : António Guterres appelle à combattre le racisme systémique
items.description: Le secrétaire général de l'ONU, António Guterres, appelle à renforcer la lutte contre le racisme systémique et les discriminations à l'occasion de la Journée internationale des personnes d'ascendance africaine, célébrée ce 31 août 2026. Il plaide pour davantage d'égalité, de justice et de changements concrets afin de garantir la pleine jouissance des droits humains aux personnes d'ascendance africaine. António Guterres salue d'abord les contributions considérables des personnes d'ascendance africaine dans de nombreux domaines, notamment la politique, les sciences, les arts, la culture, l'innovation, le sport et les affaires. Mais il souligne que ces avancées ne doivent pas masquer les obstacles qui persistent à l'exercice plein et effectif de leurs droits. Le secrétaire général des Nations unies dénonce notamment la résurgence de récits qu'il qualifie de mensongers, qui tendent à minimiser les réalités vécues par les personnes d'ascendance africaine et à effacer leur histoire. Il pointe également la persistance du racisme systémique, des inégalités sociales, des discours de haine et de la fracture numérique, qu'il relie aux survivances de l'idéologie suprématiste blanche. Pour António Guterres, la lutte contre ces injustices doit notamment passer par la reconnaissance des faits historiques et des conséquences persistantes de l'esclavage et du colonialisme, en particulier celles liées à la traite transatlantique. Il appelle également à lever les barrières qui empêchent encore de nombreuses personnes d'ascendance africaine d'exercer pleinement leurs droits et de réaliser leur potentiel. Le secrétaire général relève par ailleurs la montée des appels en faveur de la justice réparatrice et de la réparation des injustices historiques. Il considère la deuxième décennie internationale des personnes d'ascendance africaine (2025-2034) comme une nouvelle occasion d'obtenir des avancées significatives. L'ONU inscrit cette décennie autour des enjeux de reconnaissance, de justice et de développement. Pour rappel, instituée par l'Assemblée générale des Nations unies, la Journée internationale des personnes d'ascendance africaine est célébrée chaque 31 août. Elle vise notamment à promouvoir une meilleure reconnaissance du patrimoine, de la culture et des contributions des personnes d'ascendance africaine, ainsi que le respect de leurs droits humains et libertés fondamentales. Lefaso.net Source : Nations unies

items.title: Coupures électriques | Grosses pertes chez les industriels de la volaille
items.description: Les coupures intempestives d’électricité se poursuivent de manière intermittente dans toute la Tunisie. La Société tunisienne de l’électricité et du gaz (Steg) y est acculée parce que la production nationale d’électricité est aujourd’hui en-deçà de la demande. Et rien n’indique que cette situation va s’améliorer dans un avenir proche. En attendant, les citoyens, et notamment les opérateurs économiques, évaluent leurs pertes cumulées et reprochent aux autorités leur manque de planification et d’anticipation. Dans ce contexte de crise tous azimuts que vivent les Tunisiens, les éleveurs de volaille annoncent d’énormes pertes subies par leurs élevages en raison des coupures fréquentes d’électricité et des températures record enregistrées depuis la mi-juillet. Mohamed Ben Hazzaz, un éleveur de volaille de Boukrim, délégation d’El Haouaria, gouvernorat de Nabeul, a fait état, dans une déclaration à Mosaique FM , de la mort de milliers de volailles dans les élevages de cette région réputée pour cette activité qui constitue leur unique source de revenus, selon ses dires. M. Ben Hazzaz a expliqué que la situation des agriculteurs s’est aggravée en raison de la flambée des prix des groupes électrogènes à essence, passés de 3 000 à 7 000 dinars. Il a appelé l’État à intervenir pour trouver une solution et «mettre fin aux agissements des commerçants qui monopolisent la vente de ces équipements» . Il a également déploré l’absence de réaction de la part des responsables du ministère de tutelle ou de la Steg face aux difficultés rencontrées par les éleveurs de volaille. Ces derniers font face à un été caniculaire ayant entraîné la mort d’un grand nombre de volailles dans leurs élevages, ainsi que la panne — par surchauffe due à une utilisation prolongée — de plusieurs groupes électrogènes à essence. Il a qualifié les pertes subies par les industriels de «catastrophiques» . I. B. items.title: Israeli fire kills five people in Gaza, medics say
items.description: CAIRO, Aug 31 (Reuters) - Israeli airstrikes killed at least five Palestinians in the Gaza Strip on Monday, health officials said. Medics said two people were killed and several others wounded when one strike hit a crowd near the municipal public park in Gaza City, an area packed with displaced families. Later on Monday, another Israeli airstrike hit a vehicle in the Tel Al-Hawa neighbourhood in western Gaza City, killing at least three people, medics added. The Israeli military said the two attacks targeted Hamas militants, without giving further information.

items.title: Agou/Culture : La 52ᵉ édition de la fête traditionnelle « Tezan » célébrée
items.description: Agou-Gadzépé, 31 août (ATOP) – La communauté d’Agou Nyogbo Sud (commune Agou 1) a célébré, le samedi 29 août, l’apothéose de la 52ᵉ édition de la fête traditionnelle « Tezan ». La rencontre est placée sous le thème « Ensemble, engageons-nous pour de l’eau en quantité et en qualité dans le canton d’Agou Nyogbo Sud ». Elle a pour but est de valoriser des pratiques culturelles et savoir ancestraux pour leur pérennisation. « Tezan » (Fête de l’Igname) est un important rendez-vous socioculturel et communautaire du canton d’Agou Nyogbo Sud. Elle constitue un moment privilégié de retrouvailles et de rencontres des populations, des ressortissants vivant à l’intérieur du pays et de la diaspora autour des valeurs de fraternité, de solidarité, de culture, de tradition, et de développement. Cette célébration est également un espace de valorisation du patrimoine culturel local. Elle permet aux jeunes générations de mieux connaître leur histoire, leurs traditions et les valeurs qui fondent l’identité du canton. Cet événement a connu plusieurs activités, entre-autres, la journée santé environnement, les ateliers de formation des femmes et jeunes sur les activités génératrices de revenus et les formations des agriculteurs sur les cultures associées et les méfaits des engrais chimiques. Un festival «Bobobo», une caravane de sensibilisation contre l’utilisation des sachets plastiques, la défécation à l’aire libre et un tournoi de football ont marqué la commémoration. L’apothéose a été essentiellement marquée par des parades des Hamacs, la mobilisation des fonds pour le projet d’eau, les chants et danses folkloriques et la remise symbolique du trophée «Tezan» foot. Le représentant du ministre du Tourisme, de la Culture et des Arts, M. Monkli Kokou a indiqué que Tezan célèbre les prémices de l’igname, valorise le patrimoine culturel local et mobilise les filles et fils du canton autour de projets de développement communautaire. Il a ajouté que cette fête est une opportunité de promouvoir cette richesse du patrimoine culturel local afin de mieux faire connaître le canton d’Agou Nyogbo sud, tout en encourageant la consommation des produit issus de l’agriculture, de l’artisanat, ainsi que les industries culturelles, créatives et touristiques. Le président du comité d’organisation, Ange Ketor a témoigné sa gratitude aux différents acteurs aux devant desquels le chef canton d’Agou Nyogbo sud Pebi V pour les différents efforts mis à contribution permettant la réussite de cette édition. Il a invité ses frères et sœurs du canton à rester souder malgré les divergences pour construire ensemble leur milieu. Le président a souligné que le thème de cette année, traduit la volonté de faire de Tezan non seulement un moment de retrouvailles et de réjouissances, mais également un véritable instrument de développement. « Tezan est avant tout notre patrimoine. Elle est notre histoire, notre identité. A travers Tezan, nos enfants découvrent ce que nos parents et nos grands-parents ont reçu en héritage. Ils apprennent à connaître nos traditions, notre culture et les richesses de notre terroir. », a-t-il ajouté. Le chef canton d’Agou Nyogbo Sud, Togbui Pebi V, a relevé qu’ à travers Tezan, les fils et filles doivent œuvrer pour renforcer davantage les liens entre les générations, les familles, les quartiers, les villages alentours et entre toutes les composantes de leur société. Il a réaffirmé l’engagement de la chefferie traditionnelle à œuvrer aux côtés de toutes les forces vives pour la paix, l’unité et le développement de leur communauté. ATOP/BSM/MET/SED

items.title: PM Shehbaz meets Iranian President Pezeshkian on sidelines of SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Kyrgyzstan on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Council of Heads of State meeting on Monday, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). Pezeshkian welcomed PM Shehbaz in Bishkek for his three-day official visit from Aug 31 to Sep 2 and the two leaders held a meeting, the PMO said on X. Earlier, the prime minister reached the Kyrgyz Republic on a three-day official visit, from Aug 31 to Sept 2, at the invitation of President Sadyr Nurgozhoevich Zhaparov to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Council of Heads of State meeting. Adylbek Kasymaliev, chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, welcomed PM Shehbaz upon his arrival at Manas International Airport, the government’s official account on social media platform X stated . Announcing the premier’s departure, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said he would address the SCO summit and “present Pakistan’s stance on various regional and global issues”. It added that Minister of Commerce Jam Kamal Khan, Minister of Communications Abdul Aleem Khan, and Minister of Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar were accompanying PM Shehbaz. Earlier in the day, the Foreign Office had issued a statement on PM Shehbaz’s visit, saying that it would include participation in the SCO Council of Heads of State meeting, as well as bilateral engagements in the Kyrgyz Republic. “During his stay in Bishkek, the prime minister will participate in the meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of State and the SCO Plus Summit,” the statement said. “The prime minister will also assume Pakistan’s chairmanship of the SCO Council of Heads of State for 2026-2027,” it said, adding that he would also hold bilateral meetings with the leaders of the participating countries on the sidelines. PM Shehbaz will also participate in the opening ceremony of the World Nomad Games on Aug 31, the statement said. It added that on Sept 2, the prime minister would hold bilateral discussions with the Kyrgyz president on the “entire spectrum of Pakistan-Kyrgyzstan relations”. “The two sides will comprehensively review Pakistan-Kyrgyzstan relations and discuss ways to further deepen bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade and investment, energy, regional connectivity, education, tourism, and people-to-people exchanges,” it said. “The leaders will also exchange views on regional and international developments of mutual interest and cooperation at regional and multilateral fora,” it added. “Pakistan and Kyrgyzstan enjoy warm and fraternal relations, rooted in shared history, faith and cultural affinity, as well as common aspirations for peace, connectivity and prosperity in Central and South Asia,” the FO said. “The forthcoming visit will provide an important opportunity to consolidate the momentum generated by recent high-level exchanges, translate political goodwill into enhanced practical cooperation, and further strengthen the enduring partnership between Pakistan and the Kyrgyz Republic,” the statement concluded. Around a dozen world leaders will head to Bishkek to mark 25 years of the SCO, which comprises 10 member states: India, Iran, China, Pakistan, Russia, Kyrgyzstan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. The two observer states are Afghanistan and Mongolia. Pakistan is set to assume the chairmanship of the SCO’s Council of Heads of State, while next year’s CHS summit will also be hosted by Islamabad.

items.title: Mir Raza murder case: SHC reserves order on family's plea seeking JIT
items.description: KARACHI: The Sindh High Court (SHC) on Monday reserved its verdict on a plea seeking the formation of a joint investigation team (JIT) in the Mir Raza Ali murder case. Ali, a 25-year-old Karachi-based businessman, was found dead with a gunshot wound in Gulistan-i-Jauhar last month, a day after he was reported missing on July 28. His family, which has raised questions about the case’s investigation and accused authorities of trying to bury the facts, had moved the SHC last week against a decision of the provincial government to form a judicial commission and sought the formation of a JIT instead. However, authorities proceeded with the commission, with Justice Omar Sial appointed as its head. A two-member constitutional bench, headed by Justice Adnan Karim Memon, took up the family’s petition on Monday. The Sindh advocate general (AG), prosecutor general, Karachi police surgeon, police officials, the case’s investigating officer, Ali’s family, and their counsel Jibran Nasir appeared before the court during the hearing. Nasir reiterated the demand for a JIT, following which the court enquired about the difference between a JIT and a judicial commission. To that, the state’s lawyer said, “A JIT will investigate the case from various angles while a commission can provide assistance in the investigation”. Nasir reminded the court that to investigate the Gul Plaza blaze, a JIT and a commission were formed separately. He further alleged that police personnel had destroyed evidence in the case, adding that this was also mentioned in his plea. Nasir also accused police of “spreading false news through the media” and added that no statements were recorded several days after the case was registered and that the “crime scene was set on fire”. “It was set on fire to search for a bullet, just as the crime scene was washed in Rawalpindi,” he said, seemingly referring to the washing of the site of the killing of former prime minister Benazir Bhutto in 2007. He said no action was taken against the police officers “who destroyed the case and tampered with the evidence”. “We had demanded departmental action,” Nasir said, adding that it was the investigation team’s job to find the suspects. The Sindh advocate general informed the court that the “commission’s function was to investigate the negligence (in the investigation)”. Nasir maintained that “the SC has in the past also granted permission to form a JIT as well in case of administrative sabotage”. “There is sabotage at the highest level of the police in this case,” he said, recalling that police had declared the case shut “even before Ali’s grave was dug” — a reference to the exhumation of Ali’s body for a second autopsy after the Karachi police surgeon pointed out loopholes in the first post-mortem report. When the court observed that the government had already formed a commission, Nasir argued that the commission would be supported by the “same team that has failed to trace the suspects even after a month”. For his part, the Sindh AG clarified that the provincial government was “not against the family”. Following these arguments, the court reserved its order on the petition. The case The case has been mired in controversy since the beginning. While Ali’s family was convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, police had initially built the case around the possibility that he died by suicide. Days after the recovery of Ali’s body, Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed had told Geo News that the post-mortem findings in the case had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs. On August 6, a Karachi court took up an application by Ali’s father, allowed the exhumation of his body, ordered the formation of a medico-legal board for the purpose and directed that a second autopsy of Ali’s body be conducted. The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with police surgeon Dr Sumaiyya Syed as the convener. However, in the early hours of August 7, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department. While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed. But Ali’s family rejected the new board, which also resulted in the deferment of the planned exhumation on Friday. Meanwhile, the counsel for Ali’s family, Nasir accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts. The Sindh government then restored the original medical board, following which Ali’s body was exhumed on August 8. A day later, the Sindh inspector general of police’s (IG) office notified the reconstitution of the investigating team probing Ali’s death while Karachi Additional IG Azad Khan transferred the investigation into Ali’s murder to Zaman Town police station from Ferozabad Police Station, where the case was registered. The order for the probe team’s reconstitution also showed that a murder charge had been added to the first information report. The same day, the Sindh government decided to seek a judicial commission for the case’s investigation, only to defer the plan a day later after Ali’s family said they had made no such demand and had faith in the new investigation team. On Aug 19, Ali’s parents, Mir Hussain and Mariam Hussain, wrote to Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, seeking his “direct supervision of the murder investigation”. They also urged the chief minister to order an investigation and departmental inquiry into the previous investigation team and immediately suspend the officers involved. The provincial government acknowledged the letter and announced the decision on Aug 23 to form a judicial commission to determine whether the investigation in the case was being conducted impartially and to investigate the circumstances surrounding Ali’s death. However, soon after the announcement, the counsel for Ali’s family raised objections and later approached the SHC. The petition was filed on August 24 in objection to the provincial government’s decision to form a judicial commission and sought the formation of an independent and multi-agency JIT “comprising officers who have had no previous involvement in the case” in place of the commission. The commission held the first hearing on Friday, and has summoned medico-legal officer Osama Sheikh, who had performed Ali’s first autopsy. It also issued notices to the deceased’s family, their lawyer and a provincial government focal person.

items.title: Coopération internationale : Faure Gnassingbé participe au 26ᵉ sommet de l’OCS au Kirghizistan
items.description: Lomé, 31 août (ATOP) – Le Président du Conseil, Faure Gnassingbé, participe au 26ᵉ sommet de l’Organisation de la coopération de Shanghai (OCS), qui s’ouvre le lundi 31 août à Bichkek, au Kirghizistan. La rencontre est placée sous le thème « 25 ans de l’OCS : ensemble pour une paix durable, le développement et la prospérité ». Elle réunit des chefs d’État et de gouvernement de l’Eurasie autour des grands enjeux de coopération internationale. Le Togo et l’Egypte sont les deux seuls pays africains invités à ce sommet, où ils sont appelés à porter la voix de l’Afrique et à contribuer aux échanges sur les grandes questions liées à la gouvernance mondiale. Au-delà des questions économiques et géostratégiques, les travaux porteront notamment sur les mécanismes de lutte contre le terrorisme, l’extrémisme violent et la cybercriminalité dans la région. Les participants examineront également les politiques de développement des infrastructures et de connectivité, ainsi que les perspectives de création d’une architecture financière internationale indépendante. Dans le cadre des échanges sur le multilatéralisme porté par le Sud global, le Président du Conseil évoquera la situation sécuritaire dans la sous-région ouest-africaine et sur le continent africain, ainsi que la contribution du Togo à la recherche de solutions durables face à ces défis. Cette participation s’inscrit dans la dynamique de diversification des relations d’amitié et de coopération du Togo. Le pays entretient des partenariats avec plusieurs États d’Eurasie, dont la Chine, la Russie et l’Inde, dans des domaines à fort impact économique, sécuritaire et social. La présence de Faure Gnassingbé à ce rendez-vous international témoigne ainsi du positionnement stratégique du Togo et de la reconnaissance de sa diplomatie. Elle traduit également la volonté du pays de renforcer sa présence dans les grands cadres de concertation internationale et de contribuer aux discussions sur la paix, la sécurité, le développement et la coopération. Créée en 2001, l’Organisation de la coopération de Shanghai regroupe une dizaine de pays et œuvre au développement d’une coopération multiforme destinée à maintenir et à renforcer la paix, la sécurité et la stabilité dans la région. Elle entend également contribuer à l’émergence d’un nouvel ordre politique et économique international fondé sur des principes démocratiques, justes et rationnels. Dans cette dynamique d’ouverture, l’OCS cherche à établir un partenariat avec l’Union africaine (UA), fondé sur le dialogue et la promotion des intérêts communs entre les pays d’Asie et d’Afrique partageant certaines valeurs et ambitions de coopération. ATOP/AO (Source : Présidence du Conseil)

items.title: Zoundwéogo/Manga: la Délégation spéciale met en terre plus de 250 plants au lycée départemental de Manga
items.description: BURKINA-ZOUNDWEOGO-ENVIRONNEMENT-REBOISEMENT Zoundwéogo/Manga: la Délégation spéciale met en terre plus de 250 plants au lycée départemental de Manga Manga, 28 août 2026 (AIB)- La Délégation spéciale de la commune de Manga a mis en terre, vendredi, plus de 250 plants au lycée départemental de Manga, situé dans le village de Gastoèga. Cette activité s’inscrit dans le cadre de la campagne nationale de reforestation, qui se déroule du 27 juin au 30 septembre 2026, sous le thème : « Une institution, un bosquet » . Selon le directeur provincial des Eaux et Forêts du Zoundwéogo, le lieutenant-colonel Adama Kalmogo, le bosquet sera composé de plus d’une dizaine d’espèces locales, notamment des arbres d’ombrage et des espèces pouvant servir à la médecine traditionnelle. « Les élèves pourront apprendre à mieux connaître certaines espèces végétales », a-t-il indiqué, précisant que tous les plants mis en terre ont été protégés par des grilles individuelles contre notamment la divagation des animaux. Le responsable des Eaux et Forêts a également assuré que la qualité du sol du site avait été préalablement vérifiée afin de favoriser le développement des plants. Le Président de la Délégation Spéciale (PDS) de Manga, Bérenger Bihoun, a indiqué que l’initiative, financée sur fonds propres de la commune, a permis d’acquérir plus de 5 000 plants, dont 2 000 ont été remis aux écoles de la commune. « La population de Gastoèga a compris que planter un arbre, c’est sauver une vie », a déclaré l’autorité communale, saluant l’adhésion des populations au message du président du Faso, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Le choix de Gastoèga constitue également, selon le PDS, un engagement tenu, la mairie n’ayant pu y organiser sa plantation l’année précédente en raison de contraintes. Dans cette dynamique, la commune de Manga ambitionne de mobiliser au moins 50 000 plants au terme de la campagne de reforestation 2026. Au-delà de sa dimension environnementale, cette journée a constitué une occasion de renforcer la cohésion sociale en réunissant les filles et fils de la Commune de Manga, les autorités administratives, coutumières et religieuses, les services techniques, les organisations de la société civile autour des enjeux liés à la lutte contre la dégradation des terres, la désertification et les changements climatiques. Agence d’Information du Burkina BGB/bak

items.title: Motorists decry high cost of petrol in FCT
items.description: Some motorists in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) have expressed concerns over the high pump price of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), popularly known as petrol. Global oil prices rose on Monday, with Brent crude trading at about 90.35 dollars per barrel and West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude trading at about 85.35 dollars per barrel. Dangote Refinery increased its gantry price (ex-depot price) from N1,165 per litre to N1,185 per litre, and subsequently to N1,200 per litre and N1,265 per litre within the last one week. Checks by NAN on Monday showed that filling stations across the FCT had adjusted their petrol prices upward. Eterna filling station sold petrol at N1,320 per litre, Gegu Oil sold at N1,310 per litre, while Salbas Oil sold at N1,330 per litre. Other filling stations, including Nipco, sold petrol at N1,350 per litre, AY Shafa at N1,350 per litre, and TotalEnergies sold at N1,280 per litre. The development has forced motorists to pay more for the product. A motorist in Gwarinpa, Mr Olusegun Abbas, said he bought petrol at N1,320 per litre. He lamented the growing financial pressure on livelihoods caused by the soaring fuel prices. Another motorist in Dutse, Mr Adewale Salau, said he bought petrol at Gegu filling station at N1,310 per litre. He said the impact of the rising fuel cost extended beyond transportation to other aspects of livelihood. Salau described the situation as unbearable, noting that many people are struggling to cope with the ripple effects on their livelihoods. “I can not feed my children three times a day because of the high cost of things in the market. Traders complain that it is because of the increase in fuel prices. “We urge the Federal Government to urgently intervene by stabilising fuel prices,” he said. Another motorist in Kubwa, Stanley Okezie, said petrol was sold at N1,350 per litre in his area. He said that the rising cost of fuel would lead to higher food prices. Okezie said the increase in fuel prices would continue to make foodstuffs more expensive because traders would want to recover transportation costs and make a profit. He called on the Federal Government to intervene and stabilise fuel prices to ease the economic burden on Nigerians. Dr Aliyu Ilias, a development expert, also expressed concern over the hike in petrol prices, noting that the economic consequences were severe. He called on the Federal Government to act swiftly and find a lasting solution to the increase in fuel prices, save Nigerians from the stress and make the product affordable for all. Mr Chinedu Ukadike, the National Publicity Secretary of the Independent Petroleum Marketers Association of Nigeria (IPMAN), attributed the hike in petrol prices to series of adjustments by the refinery. He said Dangote Refinery had increased its gantry price from N1,165 per litre to N1,185, and subsequently to N1,200 and N1,265 within the last one week. Ukadike said marketers could not continue to sell petrol below the replacement cost. He said the frequent price changes were creating uncertainty for both marketers and consumers. items.title: The transfers to watch before window closes
items.description: The summer transfer window may have been open since 15 June but several Premier League clubs are still scrambling to get key deals over the line before Tuesday’s 23:00 BST deadline. From Julian Alvarez and Enzo Fernandez to Cody Gakpo and Ismaila Sarr, some of football’s biggest names could yet be on the move. But they will have to battle the clock to earn their dream moves before the market closes. With that in mind, BBC Sport’s football reporters have picked out the high-profile moves which could go through during what promises to be a busy ending to the window. Julian Alvarez to Barcelona or Arsenal Julian Alvarez’s potential move to Arsenal could be the biggest deal to watch, with the Atletico Madrid striker’s future now hanging in the balance. The 26-year-old is caught between his desire to leave Atletico and the club’s refusal to sell him to Barcelona. But they would do a deal with Arsenal . The Gunners have had a long-term interest in Alvarez and have been monitoring the dramatic situation, with Atleti looking for a fee of 150m euros (£128m). Alvarez has missed multiple training sessions and did not travel to face Sevilla on Saturday, with Simeone saying he wasn’t well enough. Simeone, meanwhile, has attempted to keep the door open, saying he will “do everything” he can to make Alvarez feel important when he returns to training. Enzo Fernandez to Man City Enzo Fernandez missed Sunday’s Premier League win over Brighton and his future is under increasing uncertainty, having been linked with a big-money move to Manchester City. Enzo Maresca worked with the Argentina midfielder at Chelsea and needs to bolster his ranks following the departures of Rodri, Bernardo Silva, Nico Gonzalez and Tijjani Reijnders this summer. Any potential move would likely be a club record deal, surpassing the £116m paid for Elliot Anderson earlier this summer. Lamine Camara to Chelsea Fernandez potentially leaving for Manchester City could open the door for fellow midfielder Lamine Camara to arrive at Stamford Bridge from Monaco as his replacement. It could be Chelsea’s 13th deal coming in, with exits exceeding 30 players as the Blues are expected to surpass the Premier League player sales record they set at £300m last season. There is further intrigue around departures with Mykhailo Mudryk looking for a loan move and still a lack of clarity on the futures of Pedro Neto and Tosin Adarabioyo. The likes of Dario Essugo, Deivid Washington and Shim Mheuka could also leave. Cody Gakpo to Man City or Tottenham Manchester City have opened talks with Liverpool about signing attacker Cody Gakpo and the Netherlands international is open to the move. But Liverpool would only be willing to sanction the transfer if they can bring in one more attacking player, in addition to Bradley Barcola. Spurs are also interested but City are willing to offer a deal worth around £85m and sources indicate that City is Gakpo’s preferred destination. Ismaila Sarr to Liverpool With Gakpo’s future up in the air, Liverpool have turned their attentions to Crystal Palace’s Ismaila Sarr after having two bids for Yankuba Minteh rejected by Brighton. The Seagulls want more than the £60m offered by Liverpool and it remains to be seen whether Iraola’s side go back in for him. Like the Gambian, Sarr is a right-sided winger and the Reds initially enquired about the Senegal international last week, but that was rebuffed by Crystal Palace. Richarlison to Everton and Iliman Ndiaye to Tottenham Tottenham are in advanced talks to sign Iliman Ndiaye from Everton, with Richarlison set to move in the opposite direction. Although a deal for Ndiaye is largely agreed between the two clubs, it remains unclear whether he will make the switch to north London, with Manchester City among the clubs to have expressed an interest. Everton are open to selling Ndiaye, 26, after he rejected multiple contract offers and held talks with Saudi club Al-Hilal earlier this summer. Meanwhile, Everton have agreed terms in principle to re-sign striker Richarlison after he told Spurs head coach Roberto de Zerbi “too many times that he wants to leave”. Jack Grealish to Everton Everton are growing increasingly confident of completing a loan deal to bring Jack Grealish back from Manchester City, although the precise terms of any agreement remain complicated as the England international enters the final year of his contract at Etihad Stadium. Grealish has prioritised a return to Everton, where he spent last season on loan, over the option of rejoining his boyhood club Aston Villa, who have also expressed an interest. Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Newcastle Just a few hours after the unveiling of Nico Gonzalez, Matthias Jaissle made it clear he would continue to push for further deals in the final throes of the window. Another forward is on the German’s wishlist and Newcastle have a longstanding interest in Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo, whose creativity and ability to play in a number of positions across the frontline is a huge draw. The 21-year-old also fits the age range Newcastle have targeted this summer. This would be a complicated deal to do in the final days of the window, but it was a little telling that Lille manager Davide Ancelotti left Fernandez-Pardo out of his squad for the weekend’s game against Paris St-Germain and has decided to exclude him from training until the window shuts. Joshua Zirkzee to Juventus Unless there is a very late, and unexpected, development around Marcus Rashford, it feels as if Manchester United’s deadline-day business will centre around Joshua Zirkzee and the smaller deals they can do. Fiorentina wanted to take the Netherlands forward on loan, with an option to buy. United, ideally, would prefer to sell, or at least get a loan with an obligation. With no agreement possible, Fiorentina are now looking elsewhere. However, Juventus are keen on Zirkzee, although a move for the 25-year-old hinges on Canada forward Jonathan David leaving for Atletico Madrid. Zirkzee’s exit might open the door for a left-back or a reinforcement in the forward department, although that too might initially be a loan.

Cette opération, mise en œuvre conformément aux orientations du ministère de l’Environnement, de la Pêche et du Développement Durable, vise notamment à recenser de manière exhaustive les personnels, vérifier leur présence effective à leurs postes d’affectation, contrôler leurs pièces administratives et identifier les éventuelles situations administratives irrégulières, afin de contribuer à la fiabilisation et à la mise à jour du fichier du personnel. Le directeur général a réaffirmé l’importance de cette opération pour renforcer la discipline administrative, la transparence, la gestion rationnelle des ressources humaines et l’efficacité du service public. Il a également invité l’ensemble des agents concernés à faire preuve de disponibilité, de collaboration et de responsabilité afin de permettre à la Commission de mener à bien sa mission dans les meilleures conditions. La direction générale de la Garde Forestière et Faunique, se dit engagée pour une administration plus organisée, responsable et performante. items.title: Meet 9-yr-old Nigerian girl, Charlotte teaching algebra on TikTok
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nine-year-old Charlotte Muritala from Ofa, Kwara State, has gained attention for her passion for mathematics and her efforts to teach other children through TikTok. The JSS2 student developed an interest in mathematics from a young age, saying her love for numbers has continued to grow over the years. Charlotte, in a recent interview with Channels Television, said, “I started liking mathematics since when I was small. I love mathematics because I enjoy numbers.” For the young mathematics enthusiast, solving mathematical problems is not just an academic exercise but something she genuinely enjoys. “Mathematics is fun for me. Some questions are hard, but I like solving them,” she said. Charlotte also explained how she approaches difficult questions, saying she breaks them down into smaller parts before solving them step by step. “First, I like breaking them into small part. That makes it easier for me. So I break it into small part, then I solve it,” she said. According to her, she does not give up when she encounters a difficult problem. Instead, she looks for a suitable method and works through the question gradually. “Once I start solving the hard problem, if I am not getting it, I will go and choose the best method and start solving it step by step,” Charlotte said. Her passion for mathematics has also extended to social media, where she shares what she knows with other children. Charlotte revealed that her mother created an online platform to help her reach a wider audience and share her mathematics knowledge. “My mum created another platform for me to share what I know to other children. I feel very happy and proud of myself,” she said. Charlotte’s mathematics teacher described her as an exceptional student with a strong passion for solving mathematical problems. “She is a brilliant and erudite student. Before taking someone as erudite, that means that person has exceptional skills in Mathematics,” the teacher said. The teacher added that Charlotte stands out because of her enthusiasm and ability to tackle mathematical problems. “She has passion for solving mathematical problems. In all, she is an excellent and outstanding student,” the teacher said. The teacher also called for greater support for children with exceptional academic abilities, saying qualified teachers, scholarships and proper funding could help more students develop an interest in mathematics. “If you want students to have interest in mathematics, secure the services of qualified teachers, give them scholarships and proper funding,” the teacher said. Charlotte, meanwhile, advised other children struggling with mathematics to remain persistent and learn from their mistakes. “My advice to them is to never give up. They should keep practising every day and don’t be afraid of mistakes,” she said. The post Meet 9-yr-old Nigerian girl, Charlotte teaching algebra on TikTok appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kourittenga/Compétition de belote : L’équipe de Wemtenga de Ouagadougou raffle le prix de la 8e édition
items.description: BURKINA-KOURITTENGA-JEU-SOCIETE-COMPETITION-BELOTE Kourittenga/Compétition de belote : L’équipe de Wemtenga de Ouagadougou raffle le prix de la 8e édition Koupéla, 29 août 2026 (AIB)-Le secrétaire général de la province du Kouritttenga, Fernand Wenceslas Y. N’Do, représentant le Haut-commissaire, a présidé ce samedi 29 août 2026 à Koupéla, la cérémonie de lancement de la 8e édition de compétition de belote. C’est l’équipe de Wemtenga de Ouagadougou qui a remporté le premier prix. L’activité a été organisée par l’association de Fraternité belote club de Koupéla, qui a déroulé des tables de belote venues de Ouagadougou, de Ouahigouya, de Boulsa, de Tenkodogo, de Pouytenga et de Koupéla. La huitième édition a réussi son pari, avec la table de belote de Wemtenga de Ouagadougou, sacrée championne de l’édition qui repart avec le premier prix de la compétition composé de deux maillots jaunes, un trophée et une enveloppe financière de 100 000 F CFA. Le deuxième et le troisième prix de la compétition sont revenus à la table de belote de Koupéla. Le quatrième prix a été empoché par l’une des tables de belote de Ouagadougou. La table de belote de Ouahigouya, à cette édition, a, quant à elle, reçu le prix de « Fair-Play ». Des prix de reconnaissance ont été offerts à des personnalités qui contribué à la réussite de cet évènement annuel qui dure depuis 08 ans à Koupéla. Les beloteurs de cette édition, venus de divers horizons, ont approuvé la nécessité d’une telle activité qui favorise l’esprit d’équipe, renforce les liens sociaux, contribue au raffermissement de la cohésion sociale dans ce contexte sécuritaire. « Nous sortons très satisfaits quant au déroulement de cette compétition. Nous traduisons toute notre reconnaissance à tous ceux, qui, manifestement ou dans l’anonymat, ont apporté leur soutien à la réalisation de cette compétition», a fait savoir le président du comité d’organisation Philippe Kéré. Pour le parrain de cette édition, Séraphin Kaboré, ces occasions créent un cadre sain de détente et de fraternité. « C’est des moments simples qui font naitre la solidarité et le respect mutuel qui est une valeur renforçant le vivre ensemble. Gagnez avec honneur, perdez avec sourire et surtout profitez de ce moment de fraternité pour un Burkina meilleur et paisible», a-t-il déclaré. Pour le secrétaire général de la province du Kouritttenga, Fernand Wenceslas Y. N’Do, l’activité symbolise l’engagement des filles et fils du Burkina et en particulier de la province du Kourittenga en faveur de la promotion des loisirs et d’une société plus solidaire et plus unie. Agence d’information du Burkina AWS/HB/OO

items.title: Customs seizes 204 pump-action rifles concealed in household goods at TinCan Port
items.description: By Efe Onodjae Barely three weeks after the Nigeria Customs Service intercepted a consignment of knocked-down pump-action rifle components and cannabis-infused snacks at the Tin Can Island Port, the Service has again uncovered arms shipment at the port, seizing 204 pump-action rifles concealed among household goods. The latest seizure, according to the Nigeria Customs Service, NCS, involved a 20-foot container declared as containing used household items. The container, which arrived from Turkey aboard the vessel MV Algeciras Express on August 16, 2026, was flagged for examination two days later following credible intelligence. A 100 per cent physical examination subsequently led to the discovery of the firearms concealed among furniture, refrigerators, solar panels and detergents. Speaking at the press briefing on the latest seizure, the Deputy Comptroller-General of Customs, Enforcement, Investigation and Inspection, DCG Timi Bomodi, said the 204 rifles were discovered after intelligence prompted the physical examination of the container. According to him, discrepancies import documents, particularly regarding the identity of the consignee, with investigations continuing to establish the circumstances surrounding the shipment. Bomodi said Customs experts, working with officials of the National Centre for the Control of Small Arms and Light Weapons, NCCSALW, under the Office of the National Security Adviser, ONSA, assembled the recovered firearm components. The exercise, he said, resulted in the identification of 204 MAS 49 ALTER MAGNUM pump-action rifles, alongside several leftover firearm components. The components included 39 trigger pins, 58 locking lugs, 53 charging handles, 55 pistol grip screws, 56 springs, 56 trigger groups, 38 forward grips or hand guards, 67 forward grip latches, 56 pistol grips, 54 barrels and two U-plates. Bomodi said the latest interception underscored the continued efforts by the Customs Service to frustrate attempts to smuggle firearms into Nigeria through the nation’s ports. He recalled that the Comptroller-General, Adeniyi, had during a working visit to the Tin Can Island Port Command on August 18 disclosed the earlier interception of firearm components, which were subsequently assembled into 399 pump-action rifles and handed over to the The National Centre for the Control of Small Arms and Light Weapons (NCCSALW). The Customs authorities said the latest seizure demonstrated the importance of intelligence-led enforcement, risk profiling and heightened surveillance in detecting prohibited consignments disguised as legitimate imports. “The current seizure is a further indication that the Service is maintaining heightened surveillance and intelligence-led enforcement against the illicit movement of firearms through our ports and borders,” Bomodi said. He disclosed that the seized items had been secured and documented and would be formally handed over to the NCCSALW for appropriate statutory action. Bomodi further stressed the importance of collaboration among the NCS, ONSA and other security agencies in tackling arms trafficking and related criminal activities. He warned smugglers, arms traffickers and their collaborators that Customs would continue to frustrate attempts to bring illegal firearms into the country. According to him, the Service’s risk management system, intelligence gathering, profiling and technological tools had made it increasingly difficult for prohibited items to be disguised as household goods or concealed inside containers. He said Customs was not interested only in intercepting illicit consignments but was also determined to identify the networks behind the smuggling operations. “Our objective is to expose the entire chain involved in the illicit movement of firearms, from the source and shipment to the intended destination and beneficiaries,” he said. Bomodi urged members of the trading public, particularly clearing agents with information capable of leading to the arrest of persons involved in the illegal importation of firearms, to come forward. The post Customs seizes 204 pump-action rifles concealed in household goods at TinCan Port appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sandbondtenga/Humanitaire: les acteurs s’engagent à apporter une réponse mieux coordonnée et durable
items.description: BURKINA-SANDBONDTENGA-HUMANITAIRE-REPONSE- DURABLE Sandbondtenga/Humanitaire: les acteurs s'engagent à apporter une réponse mieux coordonnée et durable Kaya, 28 août 2026 (AIB) – Les acteurs intervenant dans la réponse humanitaire dans la province du Sandbondtenga se sont engagés, vendredi à Kaya, à renforcer la coordination de leurs interventions afin de mieux répondre aux besoins des populations affectées par la crise et de préparer un relèvement durable. Organisé par la direction provinciale de la famille du Sandbondtenga, l’atelier a réuni des représentants des services techniques déconcentrés de l’État, des organisations non gouvernementales et des associations de développement, sous la présidence du haut-commissaire de la province, Idrissa Gamsonré. Les échanges ont permis de dresser un état des lieux de la situation humanitaire et de relever la persistance de besoins multisectoriels, notamment en matière d’alimentation, d’abris, de santé, d’eau, d’hygiène et d’assainissement, d’éducation, de moyens de production et de protection des personnes vulnérables. Une attention particulière a été accordée aux personnes retournées, confrontées à la destruction ou à la dégradation de leurs habitations, à la perte de leurs moyens de production et de leur cheptel, ainsi qu’à l’accès encore limité à certains services sociaux de base. « Retourner ne suffit pas. Il faut pouvoir reconstruire », a insisté le camarade Gamsonré, soulignant la nécessité de passer progressivement d’une réponse d’urgence à des solutions durables. Le haut-commissaire a plaidé pour une coordination « inclusive, participative, transparente, régulière et orientée vers les résultats », invitant les services de l’État, les collectivités, les organisations humanitaires, les ONG, les associations et les communautés à conjuguer leurs efforts. Les participants ont également été sensibilisés aux principales orientations de la Stratégie nationale de relèvement des personnes déplacées internes et des communautés d’accueil (SNR-PDICA) 2023-2027, présentée comme un cadre de référence pour accompagner la transition de l’urgence vers le relèvement. Au terme des échanges, les participants ont formulé des recommandations concrètes et opérationnelles pour améliorer l’efficacité de la réponse humanitaire. Agence d'Information du Burkina AIO/bak

items.title: Nana Kwadwo Osei Bonsu I installed as Odikro of Tepa Ankaase in Ashanti Region
items.description: The people of Tepa Ankaase in the Ahafo Ano North Municipality of the Ashanti Region have installed a new Odikro (sub-chief) to steer the affairs of the community towards unity and development. The new Odikro, known in private life as Kwadwo Osei Bonsu, was enstooled under the stool name Nana Kwadwo Addai Osei Bonsu I. He swore the Oath of Allegiance to Nana Kusi Agyapong Appau I, the Otumfuo Akwaboahene, and to the people of Ankaase on Friday, August 28, at the Akwaboah Palace. The brief but colourful traditional ceremony was witnessed by the Otumfuo Kyeamepanin, Nana Kwaku Wusu II, chiefs and elders of Akwaboah, as well as representatives of the Juabenhene. After administering the oath, Nana Kusi Agyapong Appau I advised the new Odikro to serve his people with humility, truth and dedication, and to uphold the customs and traditions of Asanteman. He also urged him to unite his people and called on residents of Tepa Ankaase to rally behind their new leader to accelerate development in the community. The Akwaboahene recounted the issues that led to the destoolment of his predecessor, noting that it was the same people who made him Odikro who later called for his destoolment. He cautioned Nana Kwadwo Osei Bonsu not to follow that path. “Your predecessor did nothing wrong to me personally, but because his own people in the community said they no longer wanted him as their Odikro, I had no option but to destool him. So do not go and bring shame upon me and the Akwaboah Stool,” the Akwaboahene stated. Nana Kusi Agyapong Appau I said the installation followed extensive consultations in line with custom and tradition, and urged residents to rally behind the new Odikro. Otumfuo Kyeamehene, Nana Kwaku Wusu II, also cautioned the new Odikro against tolerating illegal mining activities on Ankaase lands. He warned that such activities destroy farmlands and water bodies and undermine the development efforts of Asanteman, stressing that any chief who allows illegal mining would not be spared. He urged Nana Kwadwo Osei Bonsu to be vigilant and to work with the traditional council and relevant authorities to protect the lands and natural resources of the community. Nananom and opinion leaders who graced the occasion also advised the new Odikro to uphold truth, fairness and the rich cultural values of the area, and to work closely with all stakeholders for the progress of Tepa Ankaase. They also called on the youth to rally behind the new chief and eschew acts that could undermine the peace of the community. Nana Kwadwo Osei Bonsu I expressed gratitude to God for the honour bestowed upon him. He extended his appreciation to the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, and to his overlord, Nana Kusi Agyapong Appau I, for their blessings and for confirming his enstoolment. He further thanked the Kingmakers for the confidence reposed in him and the people of Ankaase for their love and support, pledging to work diligently to meet their expectations. He urged his people to live in harmony, respect one another, respect traditional authority, and remain law-abiding as he works to improve their living standards. Although Ankaase has been plagued by chieftaincy-related violence in recent times, the enstoolment of Nana Kwadwo Osei Bonsu I witnessed a massive turnout of community members at the Akwaboahene’s Palace, who gathered to witness his oath of allegiance and declare their unflinching support for him. Reflecting on the previous incidents, he urged residents to let go of the past and embrace unity to foster development. “Development is my priority for the Ankaase community, and for that matter, I am urging you all to support me in a peaceful manner to achieve this goal. I am Odikro for all the people of Ankaase,” he said. Nana Kwadwo Osei Bonsu I called on all factions and residents, both home and abroad, to come together and support his vision to transform Ankaase, particularly in the areas of education, health, youth employment and infrastructure. “My reign will focus on unity, youth empowerment and development. I call on all sons and daughters of Ankaase, both home and abroad, to come together so we can build a better future for the next generation,” he said. Some of the residents expressed optimism that the new Odikro’s leadership would attract development projects, improve education and enhance communal living in the area.

items.title: ‎2027: Tinubu, Ododo deserves second term – Kogi ex-speaker
items.description: ‎By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja ‎ ‎Former Speaker of the Kogi State House of Assembly, Matthew Kolawole, has urged the people of Kabba-Bunu/Ijumu Federal Constituency to support the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Kogi State Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo in the 2027 general elections. ‎ ‎Kolawole made the call at the weekend while speaking at an endorsement and mega rally organised by the Team Yomi Kola political structure in Kabba, where APC supporters across Kabba-Bunu and Ijumu Federal Constituency rallied behind the two leaders. ‎ ‎The gathering attracted party leaders, elders, women and youth groups, with Kolawole describing the event as an opportunity for the people to assess the performance of the Tinubu and Ododo administrations and determine whether their policies and programmes deserved continuity. ‎ ‎He urged the people to objectively assess the policies and programmes of the two administrations, saying responsible citizenship required acknowledging areas of progress while constructively drawing attention to areas requiring improvement. ‎ ‎Highlighting some of the Federal Government’s initiatives, the former Speaker cited the Students Loan Scheme and various youth and women empowerment programmes targeted at expanding access to education, entrepreneurship, skills acquisition and employment. ‎ ‎He also identified the ongoing reconstruction of the Kabba-Egbe-Ilorin road as a strategic infrastructure project capable of boosting commercial activities and strengthening connectivity between Kogi, Kwara and neighbouring states. ‎ ‎On security, Kolawole commended the Federal Government for strengthening the nation’s security architecture through increased support for the armed forces and other security agencies in the fight against banditry, kidnapping and other criminal activities. ‎ ‎Turning to Kogi State, he praised Governor Ododo for prioritising security, workers’ welfare and infrastructure, noting that collaboration between government and community-based security structures had contributed to improved safety in parts of Okunland previously affected by criminal activities. ‎ ‎Kolawole also commended the state government’s regular payment of salaries and pensions, describing the policy as critical to the welfare of workers and pensioners and an important contributor to grassroots economic activity. ‎ ‎He described the establishment and development of Kogi State University, Kabba, as a landmark investment in human capital development, saying the institution would have far-reaching benefits for the people of Okunland and the state. ‎ ‎The former Speaker further lauded the payment of WAEC and NECO examination fees for students in public schools, saying the initiative had reduced the financial burden on parents while helping to widen access to education. ‎ ‎He, however, stressed that government performance must ultimately be measured by its impact on the daily lives of citizens, identifying roads, healthcare, electricity, water supply, agriculture and support for small businesses as areas requiring sustained attention. ‎ ‎The rally climaxed with the unanimous endorsement of President Tinubu, Governor Ododo and other APC candidates, as party supporters pledged their loyalty and support ahead of the 2027 elections. ‎ ‎Also speaking, the Special Adviser to Governor Ododo on Security, Jerry Omadara, said the achievements recorded by the Tinubu and Ododo administrations during their first tenure justified their re-election in 2027. ‎ ‎Omadara urged the electorate to support both leaders for continuity, saying another term would provide them the opportunity to consolidate their programmes and deliver more dividends of democracy to Nigerians. ‎ ‎Kolawole, while calling for unity and peaceful political participation, expressed optimism that continued cooperation among stakeholders would produce a more secure, prosperous and developed Kabba-Bunu/Ijumu Federal Constituency, Kogi State and Nigeria. ‎ The post ‎2027: Tinubu, Ododo deserves second term – Kogi ex-speaker appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: FDA, National Security arrest suspect over sale of cigarette-shaped sweets
items.description: The Food and Drugs Authority (FDA), in collaboration with National Security, has seized quantities of an unregistered cigarette-shaped confectionery branded Cigarette Rod Lollipop from the Central Business District of Accra. According to a press release issued on Monday, August 31, the seizure was made over the weekend during a crackdown on the sale of the product. A key suspect believed to be at the centre of its sale has been arrested and placed in police custody as investigations continue into its importation, distribution and sale. The FDA said the product has not been registered with the Authority, meaning its composition is unknown and could pose public health risks to consumers. The regulator also raised concerns about the sweets’ cigarette-like appearance, particularly their potential influence on children. “Children holding and using the cigarette-shaped candy could usher them into the habit of smoking,” the FDA warned, saying the product could undermine Ghana’s national campaign against smoking. READ ALSO: FDA storms Makola Market, arrests traders over sale of ‘cigarette toffee’ The Authority has therefore urged consumers not to purchase or use the Cigarette Rod Lollipop under any circumstances. The FDA further reminded traders that the sale of unregistered food products is prohibited under Section 97(1) of the Public Health Act, Act 851, 2012. The law makes it an offence to manufacture, import, export, distribute, sell or supply food, or expose food for sale, unless the product has been registered by the Authority. The FDA has appealed to anyone who has the product in stock to contact the Authority immediately or submit it to the nearest FDA office. It is also asking the public to report anyone selling the sweets or other suspected unregistered products. Anyone with credible information leading to the arrest of the importers or others involved in the product’s importation and distribution will be treated confidentially and rewarded. “Every such information provided will be treated with strict confidentiality and shall be handsomely rewarded,” the FDA said. Members of the public can contact the FDA on 055 111 2224 / 055 111 2225 or by email at fda@fda.gov.gh.

items.description: BURKINA-SANDBONDTENGA-SOLIDARITÉ-DON-FDS-VDP Sandbondtenga/Solidarité: Barsalogho Koamba International offre des vivres et du carburant aux forces engagées pour la sécurité Barsalogho, 29 août 2026 (AIB) – L’Association Barsalogho Koamba International a remis, samedi, deux tonnes de riz aux Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP) et 200 litres de carburant au détachement de gendarmerie de Barsalogho, dans le cadre d’une initiative de solidarité couplée à une campagne de reboisement. D’une valeur totale estimée à 2 100 000 FCFA, le don a été effectué, selon les donateurs, en réponse à un appel du président de la Délégation spéciale (PDS) de Barsalogho en faveur des forces engagées dans la sécurisation de la commune. « C’est pour répondre à l’appel du PDS en faveur des VDP que nous avons agi. Nous comptons renouveler ce genre d’actions », a-t-il affirmé Jérôme Sawadogo,, président de l'association donatrice. Pour eux, ce don traduit la volonté de la jeunesse de Barsalogho, à travers l’Association, de contribuer aux efforts de sécurisation et de restauration de la paix dans la commune. « Ce geste nous encourage à nous battre davantage pour la sécurité de la commune », a déclaré Abdoulaye Ouédraogo, porte-parole des VDP bénéficiaires. Le président de la délégation spéciale de Barsalogho, Sansan Mathias Palé en recevant le don en présence des autorités coutumières, a salué cette initiative de solidarité et invité les autres associations de la commune à suivre cet exemple en apportant leur contribution aux efforts de paix et de développement. L’Association Barsalogho Koamba International a également marqué son adhésion à la politique de reverdissement du Burkina Faso par une opération de reboisement. Le reboisement a débuté dans la cour royale de Naaba Guiguemdé où deux plants ont été mis en terre, avant de se poursuivre au Centre médical avec antenne chirurgicale (CMA) et à la mairie de Barsalogho.
